title: Opera: Persistent Verbal Critic for Coding Agents

beats.text: Why do 50% of your GPU cycles waste compute before Opera fixes the bottleneck?

beats.text: The villain? Transient feedback. It’s a manager shouting instructions, then vanishing before the worker actually finishes the job.
beats.visual_focus: A ghost-like critic icon fading away while the agent repeats the same error.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: Finally, a script that doesn't treat me like a toddler. The 'goldfish' analogy actually lands because I've spent hours watching Cursor or Copilot loop on the same syntax error. You didn't use any 'smart drawer' nonsense, and you got straight to the point. I actually care about the 15% jump because you tied it to SWE-Bench, which is a metric I actually recognize.

thriller_metadata.physical_analogy: A manager shouting instructions at a worker, then walking away before the task is actually finished.
thriller_metadata.paradigm_shift: From reactive guessing to systematic, evidence-based resolution
